summary: The Sergeant Dave Crete FORGOTTEN Veterans Act of 2026 is a bill to improve benefits, healthcare tracking, and recognition for military veterans who may have been exposed to toxic substances or radiation while serving at specific covered locations, including the Nevada Test and Training Range, the Nevada National Security Site, and designated Energy Employees Occupational Illness Compensation Program Act facilities.

affected_groups.effect: Benefit from identification processes, presumption of toxic exposure and radiation-risk activities, inclusion in a new veteran registry, and potential improvements in claims adjudication and healthcare delivery.
affected_groups.group: Veterans who served at covered locations (including the Nevada Test and Training Range, Nevada National Security Site, a

affected_groups.effect: Must coordinate to identify affected veterans, share information and documentation, establish registries, and carry out or fund required studies.
affected_groups.group: Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) and Department of Defense (DoD)

key_provisions: Requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs and the Secretary of Defense to establish a process to identify veterans who served at covered locations and may have encountered toxic exposure, without requiring affirmative evidence of specific toxic substances if service at the location is established.
Treats service and onsite participation within the Nevada Test and Training Range and Nevada National Security Site from January 27, 1951 onward as radiation-risk activities for VA purposes.

Establishes a presumption of toxic exposure and service connection for certain diseases for veterans assigned to duty stations at covered Department of Energy facilities or the Nevada Test and Training Range and Nevada National Security Site.
Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to arrange a scientific study regarding potential toxic exposures, chemical hazards, and cancer rates among veterans who served at covered locations.

Mandates the establishment and maintenance of a veteran registry by the Department of Veterans Affairs to collect health data, verify service, inform veterans of benefits, and support research, with an option for veterans to opt out.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to classify the Nevada Test and Training Range, Nevada National Security Site, and certain DOE facilities as locations where contamination occurred, and to identify service members stationed there.
missing_information: The exact number of veterans who will be affected or identified by the new registry and identification processes.
The specific cost or appropriations required to carry out the studies, registries, and expanded benefit provisions.

summary_detail.significance: The bill addresses potential health and benefit gaps for military personnel who served in specific toxic or radiological test environments, modifying how the federal government tracks exposures and establishes service connections for disability and healthcare claims.
